metadata.title: Secure Software Development Lifecycle (SDLC) Core

props.name: capability
props.remarks: Business capability for governing creation and delivery of software artifacts without granting deployment or execution authority.

props.name: technology-domain
props.remarks: Software factories, CI/CD systems, infrastructure-as-code, configuration and policy-as-code, and delivery pipelines.

props.name: architecture-pattern
props.remarks: Foundational Zero Trust SDLC pattern defining scope, legitimacy, and non-equivalence rules for software delivery.

props.name: data-pattern
props.remarks: Defines SDLC artifacts, provenance, attribution, and assurance evidence as trust-relevant data.

props.name: nist-controls
props.value: SA, CM, IA, AU, SI, SR
props.remarks: SDLC Core interprets but does not implement these control families.

metadata.remarks: SDLC Core defines what constitutes legitimate software delivery under Zero Trust principles. It governs application code, scripts, infrastructure-as-code, configuration, and policy-as-code. This pattern establishes explicit non-equivalence between build, test, approval, and deployment.

components.title: SDLC Scope and Legitimacy
components.description: Defines which software delivery activities, artifacts, and pipelines are in scope for Secure-SDLC governance.

components.title: Unified SDLC Artifact Coverage
components.description: Treats software code, scripts, configuration, infrastructure-as-code, and policy-as-code as governed SDLC artifacts.

techniques.name: Stage Capabilities
techniques.remarks: Staging malicious code, scripts, or IaC artifacts in the build environment.

techniques.name: Artifact Verification
techniques.remarks: Verification of artifact integrity and provenance.

components.title: SDLC Non-Equivalence Constraints
components.description: Defines what SDLC signals do not grant or imply (e.g., build success ≠ deploy permission).

components.title: SDLC Boundary Definition
components.description: Defines the boundary between SDLC delivery and runtime deployment or execution.

techniques.name: Subvert Trust Controls
techniques.remarks: Attempt to treat SDLC output as implicit deployment authority.

techniques.name: Authorization Enforcement
techniques.remarks: Explicit separation of delivery and deployment authority.
